speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a fever, runny nose, and headache; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started and if you have had any close contact with others who are sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The timeline is classic for this condition: prodromal viral symptoms (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by the characteristic "slapped cheek" facial rash, and finally the lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities that often appears days later. No further testing is required as the clinical presentation is definitive.
